newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond ylds up, easing left to another day.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond ylds up, easing left to another day.

text.p: *Australian bond yields remained higher as long positions were lightened in the wake of no monetary policy change by the Reserve Bank and after the strong gains in recent days.
*Rate cut now seen more likely after August board meeting.
Australian bond yields remained higher at noon on Friday as long positions were lightened after the Reserve Bank made no monetary policy announcement and after the strong gains in recent days.

The market had fully priced a 50 basis point easing in the 5.5 percent official cash rate after this week's benign inflation and wages data, although the most likely date is now seen after the August 5 board meeting, analysts said.
"We do get some economic data next week, but those numbers are not expected to be strong enough to rule out any rate cut," said David Bassanese, senior economist at Bankers Trust.
Data next week includes June and June quarter retail trade and June building approvals.
September bill futures eased to a low of 94.93, although this still equates to a cash rate of 5.07 percent and still leaves a 1/2 point cut largely priced in.

Ten-year bond futures also wound back from Thursday's all-time high of 93.640, although technical analysts say the outlook only starts to turn mildly negative on a break down through 93.470 and a retest of the peak still remains a possiblity.

The market's weaker tone saw spreads give up some ground to the dollar bloc after Thursday's tightening. The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread made a strong test of 25 basis points on Thursday, its lowest level since the early 1980s. New Zealand bonds were supported by strength in the N.Z. TWI.
